name: Alamandine

lead: Alamandine is a small peptide made in the body as part of the renin-angiotensin system, described in 2013. Longevity-minded readers discuss it for heart, vessel and tissue protection.

It is generated by ACE2 from angiotensin A or from angiotensin-(1-7) and signals mainly through the MrgD receptor, producing vasorelaxation and protection against cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in animals. Evidence comes from cell and rodent experiments; no human trials have tested it.

paras: There is no approved product or established routine. It is listed among longevity-category peptides.
No human safety data exist. Because it influences blood pressure and vascular tone in animals, effects in people are unstudied. It is not an approved drug.

angle.text: Alamandine is a renin-angiotensin peptide that lowers blood pressure and protects heart tissue in rodents, so longevity-minded readers discuss it for heart and vessel health. It has not been tested in humans, and no appearance use exists.

lead: Alamandine is a heptapeptide of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), the hormone network that regulates blood pressure, fluid and electrolyte balance. It was characterised in 2013 and is formed from angiotensin A by ACE2, or directly from angiotensin-(1-7).[1][2]

It acts mainly through the MrgD receptor and, in laboratory studies, produces effects that oppose those of angiotensin II, such as vasorelaxation and protection against cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in animals.[1][2] Published work is preclinical; no human clinical trial of alamandine as a treatment was found, and no source reviewed documents appearance-related use.[2]

paras: The 2013 Circulation Research paper reported identification of alamandine by mass spectrometry, showed that it circulates in human blood, and described its generation by ACE2 from angiotensin A or from angiotensin-(1-7).[1] Wikipedia notes that an earlier 2007 report had detected the peptide in human plasma.[2]

Reviews place alamandine in the protective arm of the RAS alongside ACE2, angiotensin-(1-7) and the Mas receptor, whose actions generally counteract angiotensin II in the heart, kidney and vasculature.[3][4][5] Related work examines the MAS-related receptor family to which MrgD belongs.[6]

According to the encyclopedia summary of the literature, alamandine produced endothelium-dependent vessel relaxation, lowered blood pressure in hypertensive rats, and reduced cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in mice under pressure overload; mice lacking MrgD developed dilated cardiomyopathy. These results come from cells and rodents.[2]

No studies found. Published research on alamandine consists of laboratory and animal studies; the encyclopedia entry reports higher circulating levels in people with end-stage renal disease, which is an observation rather than a treatment trial.[2]

timeline.event: Peptide first detected in human plasma by mass spectrometry (per Wikipedia).[2]
Alamandine characterised as a new RAS component.[1]
